title: Company Dinner (hoesik)
description:
The team leader sent a group chat message:
'Team dinner tonight! Please try to make it :)'

[Hoesik is mandatory-in-spirit company group dining. It's not just dinner — it's a loyalty ritual. Leaving early signals disengagement. Staying until the end, drinking even if you don't want to, means you're 'one of us.' In Korean corporate culture, the after-hours bond often matters more than desk performance.]

No question mark. A request that's nearly impossible to refuse.
Samgyeopsal restaurant, second round at noraebang (karaoke room), third round at a pojangmacha (outdoor tent bar).

choices.text: Stay until the end — go with the team flow
choices.result_text:
Past midnight. Had drinks, sang karaoke.

Came home with a heavy body — but the team leader clapped me on the shoulder. 'Good work tonight.'
In Korean workplaces, trust sometimes gets built exactly this way.

choices.text: Just the first round — slip out early
choices.result_text:
'I have something early tomorrow.' Left after the samgyeopsal.

The team leader said 'go ahead.' Hard to read the expression.
How to take that look — still not sure.

title: Working Late
description:
7 PM. Past quitting time.
The team leader is still at their desk.

You read the room. The unspoken rule of Korean offices:
if the boss is still there, leaving first is hard.

choices.text: Outlast them — leave after the team leader
choices.result_text:
10 PM — the team leader finally got up. Left after.

Got back to the goshiwon close to midnight.
Tonight's overtime wasn't about work. It was about reading the room.

'you'll head out now.' And left.

Felt eyes on your back — but it faded as you walked.
Your time is yours to keep. That takes practice too.

title: Kkondae
description:
The team leader said it again.
'Back when I was your age...'

[Kkondae is a Korean term for someone — usually older — who imposes their experience and values on juniors as absolute truths. Not just any old-timer: specifically someone who refuses to accept that times have changed, and uses seniority to shut down new ideas. The word has become a cultural shorthand for Korea's generational workplace tension.]

Seniority doesn't always mean being right — but pushing back isn't easy.

choices.text: 'You're absolutely right' — let it wash over you
choices.result_text:
Agreed along. The team leader looked satisfied.

You thought differently — but you held it back today.
Whether this is pragmatism or surrender — you still don't know where the line is.

choices.text: Politely say what you actually think
choices.result_text:
'Your thinking is a bit different — here's why...' Carefully.

The team leader paused. 'Hmm, that's worth considering.'
Better than expected. Courage takes practice.

title: Office Politics
description:
Factions have formed in the team.
The team leader's camp and the deputy leader's camp.

Who you eat lunch with signals your allegiance.
Having to think about this on top of everything else — exhausting.

choices.text: Stay neutral — keep both sides at arm's length
choices.result_text:
Team leader's side today, deputy's side tomorrow.

Best I can do for now.
Someday I'll have to pick a side — but that's a problem for then.

choices.text: Decide to get out of this dynamic through performance
choices.result_text:
Chose not to spend energy on the faction war.

Focused on results instead. Strong work survives any faction.
That wasn't wrong — at least for now.

title: Salary Negotiation
description:
Annual review season.
HR has scheduled a one-on-one.

Most Korean workers don't negotiate their salary.
The culture of 'take what's given' runs deep.

choices.text: Come prepared with data and ask for a raise
choices.result_text:
'Based on last year's performance metrics and market rates, you'd like to request a 15% increase.'

HR looked caught off guard. Settled at 7%.
Nothing changes if you don't ask.

choices.text: 'I leave it to you' — accept the company's decision
choices.result_text:
3% increase. The company's call.

Fine. But you also know you can't keep doing this.
You'll prepare properly next year.
